boundary: zou_he_velocity_inlet(x=0) + zou_he_pressure_outlet(x=nx-1) + half-way bounce-back at ellipse wall (post-streaming)
comparison_method: s^Q: area-equivalent scale of the digital staircase ellipse from the measured flow rate, s^Q = sqrt(2*Q/(pi*a*b*U_max)), U_max = 2*u_in imposed; a_eff = a*s^Q, b_eff = b*s^Q (the exact analog of R_eff^Q for the circular pipe). The staircase half-way bounce-back ellipse is physically NOT the continuous ellipse of semi-axes (a,b); s^Q is an independent integral observable (not fitted to the profile). Nominal (a,b) and 2-parameter profile fits (a_fit, b_fit, diagnostic only) are reported for reference.
primary_metric: max relative error of the lam-binned (elliptically-averaged) profile in the central region (|u_ana| > 0.2*U_max), vs u(y,z)=U_max*(1-lam/s^Q^2), lam = (y/a)^2 + (z/b)^2, U_max = 2*u_in imposed
notes: s^Q-corrected comparison: per-bin elliptically-averaged profile max (abs U_max=2*u_in): 5.11% -> 2.43% — NOT both <=3%, monotone grid convergence, s^Q = 1.01126 / 1.00510 (a_eff = 20.225 / 40.204), b_eff = 10.113 / 20.102). Per-cell (stricter) central max: 15.86% -> 6.18% (staircase transition layer, first-order in 1/a; disclosed, secondary). Shape-normalized per-bin: 7.24% -> 3.36% (disclosed). Nominal (a,b) per-bin reference: 11.81% -> 5.95%. No extrapolation, no tuning. Diagnosis: the digital staircase ellipse wall is ANISOTROPIC — its hydraulic geometry cannot be represented by a single scale factor. Profile-fit effective semi-axes: (a_fit-a, b_fit-b) = (+1.18, -0.15) / (+1.06, -0.15); the major-axis end (single-cell staircase tip, radius of curvature ~b^2/a) bulges outward by ~1.1 cells while the minor axis pinches by ~-0.15 cells, versus the circular pipe's isotropic +0.11. The s^Q single-scale comparison therefore fails in the outermost central lambda-bin at a=20 (5.11%) and the same bin drops to 2.43% at a=40 (first-order in 1/a). The measured profile is nonetheless an exact elliptic parabola (fit residual <0.2%), confirming solver/BC correctness — the failure is the single-parameter reference geometry, not the simulation.
